title: Camellia Answer
description: A melody appears inside the right hand beneath a sustained upper light, then is answered by the left hand. The C–E-flat–D–G thought descends from Camellia Viaduct. Four exchanges change the answering harmony; the final phrase leaves C minor for a quiet E-flat added-sixth chord.
difficulty: Advanced three-voice phrasing and hand-to-hand melody exchange
technical_note: Keep the RH upper notes softer than its moving inner voice. The first LH answer is exactly an octave below the first inner phrase. Hidden full-bar inner rests occur only while the upper voice sounds; the melody changes hands every three bars.

performance.note: The inner melody should be clearly heard beneath the held upper notes. Each answer inherits its phrase shape, while the harmonic background changes gently.

composition_time_source: Recorded when the first score was saved.

audio_reverb.description: Subtle warm room; preserve the clarity of moving voices.
